title: Grace that makes pleasing does not precede God's love
source_text: XLIV. Alteram vero gratiae speciem Doctores iidem non ideo nominant gratiam gratum facientem, quod praecedat omnem actum dilectionis divinae erga nos, & sit causa qua Deus primum movetur ut nobis bene velit; id quod Reformati merito falsum & absurdum judicant: cum Deus prius diligat nos, quam illum diligamus.
pass_a_gloss: XLIV. But the other species of grace the same Doctors do not therefore name grace making pleasing, because it should precede every act of divine love toward us, and be the cause by which God first is moved that he may will well to us; which the Reformed rightly judge false and absurd: since God loves us before we love him.
pass_b_english: Thesis XLIV. When these doctors name the other species grace that makes pleasing, their reason is not that it precedes every act of divine love toward us, or that it is the cause by which God is first moved to wish us well.
The Reformed rightly judge that to be false and absurd, since God loves us before we love him.
